issues.legal_issue: Acquisition proceedings lapse when an award was made at least five years before the new acquisition law commenced and either possession was not taken or compensation was not paid.
material_facts: The acquisition awards were made more than five years before the new law commenced.
The High Court found that possession had not been taken and compensation had not been paid.
The High Court declared the acquisitions lapsed, and the acquiring authorities appealed.
issues.conclusion: The acquisitions had lapsed, and the appeals were dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 24(2) of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013, applies sequentially: the existence of an award under Section 11 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, made at least five years before commencement of the 2013 Act must first be established; then, proof that either possession was not taken or compensation was not paid attracts lapse. The Court relied on Pune Municipal Corporation v. Harakchand Misirimal Solanki, Union of India v. Shiv Raj, Bimla Devi v. State of Haryana, and Rajiv Chowdhrie HUF v. Union of India.

rule.if: section_24_lapse_proceeding and award_at_least_five_years_old and (possession_not_taken or compensation_not_paid)

predicates.section_24_lapse_proceeding: A party sought a determination that existing land acquisition proceedings had lapsed under the new acquisition-law transition provision.
predicates.award_at_least_five_years_old: The acquiring authority made an award at least five years before the new acquisition law commenced.
predicates.possession_not_taken: The acquiring authority had not taken possession of the acquired land.
predicates.compensation_not_paid: The acquiring authority had not paid compensation for the acquired land.
predicates.acquisition_proceedings_deemed_lapsed: The acquisition proceedings are treated as having lapsed.

issues.definition: When a lapse determination concerns existing acquisition proceedings, the award is at least five years old, and either possession was not taken or compensation was not paid, the proceedings are treated as lapsed.

issues.legal_issue: A later ordinance cannot retrospectively remove a landholder's accrued statutory right under the acquisition-law transition provision.
material_facts: An ordinance issued after the transition provision had conferred rights on landholders added a proviso concerning possession not taken because of interim orders.
The Court had previously held that the ordinance operated prospectively and agreed with that interpretation in this judgment.
issues.conclusion: The ordinance operates prospectively and does not retrospectively take away an accrued statutory right.
issues.legal_principle: The right conferred on landholders by Section 24(2) of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013, is statutory and cannot be taken away by an ordinance inserting a proviso without retrospective effect. The Court relied on Radiance Fincap (P) Ltd. v. Union of India, and noted the subsequent reiteration of that position in Arvind Bansal v. State of Haryana and Karnail Kaur v. State of Punjab.

predicates.landholder_acquisition_right_proceeding: A proceeding concerns a landholder's statutory right relating to an existing land acquisition.
predicates.statutory_right_already_accrued: The landholder's statutory right arose before the later ordinance was made.
predicates.later_ordinance_adds_limitation: A later ordinance adds a limitation that would restrict the previously conferred right.
predicates.later_ordinance_does_not_retroactively_r: The later ordinance does not take away the previously accrued right retrospectively.

issues.definition: When a landholder's statutory right has already accrued in an acquisition proceeding and a later ordinance adds a limitation, the ordinance does not remove that right retrospectively.
